options.details: General Purpose tier, provisioned, Gen5 (or standard-series), 8 vCore, zone redundant, 250 GB, locally redundant backups within EU
options.rationale: General Purpose drops the Business Critical 3-4x premium while still giving zone redundancy and the same compute for a ~5,000-user booking app.

Needs a check that IOPS/log throughput fit the workload

options.details: General Purpose serverless, zone redundant, min 2 / max 8 vCore, auto-pause disabled, ~40% active (peaks 9-18h), 250 GB
options.rationale: Serverless bills compute per second and scales down overnight and off-peak, so you pay for 8 vCore only during business-hours peaks.
tradeoffs: Cold-start/scale-up latency on load spikes
Per-vCore rate is higher while active
Only pays off if utilisation is really low off-hours

meters.product: SQL Database General Purpose - Serverless - Compute Gen5
meters.why: Serverless Gen5 compute billed per vCore actively used; assumed peak max 8 vCore during ~40% of the month (auto-pause disabled; min 2 vCore idle not separately priced here).

options.details: Premium v3 P1v3, Linux, 2 instances (or 1 instance plus autoscale to 2 during 9:00-18:00)
options.rationale: P2v3 is likely oversized for 5,000 users; P1v3 halves the compute cost while keeping 2 instances for availability.
tradeoffs: Half the CPU/RAM per instance, so load testing is needed
Less headroom for peak bursts
options.effort_reason: Same PaaS model, smaller SKU and config change

meters.product: Azure App Service Premium v3 Plan - Linux
meters.why: P1v3 Linux plan, 2 instances running all month, same as today's always-on setup.

options.details: Consumption plan (Linux), nightly timer trigger, ~20 min run, functionTimeout up to 10 min, use Durable Functions or split into chunks if needed
options.rationale: A 20-minute nightly job uses about 0.7 hours/day of compute, so pay-per-execution costs a few dollars versus an always-on EP1.
tradeoffs: 10-minute default/max timeout forces chunking or Durable Functions
No VNet integration, so private access to SQL is not possible
Cold starts

meters.product: Functions
meters.why: Assumed nightly run of 20 min (30 nights) at 1.5 GB average memory: 30*1200s*1.5 = ~54,000 GB-s; rounded estimate of 2,400 is wrong; using ~54000 below instead.

meters.product: Functions
meters.why: One timer execution per night, ~30 a month (plus chunking would add a few; assumed ~30).

options.details: Container Apps job (scheduled, cron nightly), 1 vCPU 2 GiB, ~20 min per run, consumption plan
options.rationale: A scheduled job bills only for the ~20 minutes it runs and has no execution time limit, unlike an always-ready Premium instance.
tradeoffs: Needs the code containerised
Needs a Container Apps environment and registry
options.effort_reason: Container build, job conversion and new platform adoption for a team without Kubernetes experience

meters.product: Azure Container Apps
meters.why: Nightly job of 20 min at 1 vCPU: 30 runs x 1200 s = 36,000 vCPU-seconds.

meters.product: Azure Container Apps
meters.why: 2 GiB memory for 36,000 seconds = 72,000 GiB-seconds.

options.details: Standard tier C1 (1 GB), sessions only
options.rationale: Session data for ~5,000 users fits easily in 1 GB, and C1 Standard keeps the replicated SLA at about half the cost of C2.
tradeoffs: Less memory and bandwidth headroom
Resizing needed if session size grows
options.effort_reason: Same managed cache, smaller tier; minor config change

meters.product: Azure Redis Cache Standard
meters.why: Standard C1 cache, one instance all month.

options.details: Blob Storage, Cool access tier, LRS, ~500 GB invoices (PDF), lifecycle rule to Cool after 30 days
options.rationale: Invoice PDFs are rarely read after the first weeks, so Cool storage cuts the per-GB cost.
tradeoffs: Higher read and transaction charges
30-day minimum retention charge
Saves only a few dollars/month
options.effort_reason: Same managed storage; add lifecycle rule and tier change

meters.why: ~500 GB invoices stored in Cool LRS (same volume as today).

rejections.reason: The nightly invoice job runs ~20 minutes but the Consumption plan caps function execution at 10 minutes maximum.

Serverless GP scaling and resume behaviour risks latency for a production workload with 9-18h peaks, though auto-pause is disabled so this rule is only marginally relevant; the 4 vCore SKU is a downsize from 8 vCore requirement.

plans.name: Cheapest
plans.summary: Takes the lowest price on every component in North Europe, with the biggest saving coming from moving the database to PostgreSQL Flexible Server. It also downsizes App Service and Redis and moves the nightly job to Container Apps.
tradeoffs: Moving from SQL Server to PostgreSQL needs a schema and query migration off T-SQL, and only works if the app isn't tied to SQL Server features
App Service P1v3 and Redis C1 give less peak headroom and need load testing
The invoice job must be containerised
Cool storage has higher read charges and a 30-day minimum for only a few dollars saved
PostgreSQL runs at 4 vCore versus 8 vCore today, so performance must be validated
plans.note: Moving everything to swedencentral would save only $12.20/mo more (1.2%), not enough to justify a region migration, so this plan stays in northeurope.

suggestions: Move SQL from Business Critical 8 vCore to General Purpose 4-6 vCore (keep zone redundancy). Business Critical is the largest cost driver (~$3,000+/mo); General Purpose zone-redundant with right-sized vCores typically cuts this by 50-60%. Check CPU/IO metrics first and consider serverless or reserved capacity.
Buy 1-year Azure Reservations/Savings Plan for the steady-state resources (SQL vCores, App Service P2v3 instances). This typically saves 30-40% with no architecture change.
Replace the always-on Functions EP1 with a Consumption or Flex Consumption plan, since the nightly invoice job runs only ~20 min. This saves ~$150/mo.
Right-size App Service to P1v3 x2 (or autoscale 1-2 instances outside 9:00-18:00) and move invoice PDFs older than ~90 days to Cool tier storage. This is a smaller saving but low risk.

suggestions: Move SQL from Business Critical 8 vCore to General Purpose 4-6 vCore (keep zone redundancy). Business Critical is the largest cost driver (~$3,000+/mo); General Purpose zone-redundant with right-sized vCores typically cuts this by 50-60%. Check CPU/IO metrics first and consider serverless or reserved capacity.
Buy 1-year Azure Reservations/Savings Plan for the steady-state resources (SQL vCores, App Service P2v3 instances). This typically saves 30-40% with no architecture change.
Replace the always-on Functions EP1 with a Consumption or Flex Consumption plan, since the nightly invoice job runs only ~20 min. This saves ~$150/mo.
Right-size App Service to P1v3 x2 (or autoscale 1-2 instances outside 9:00-18:00) and move invoice PDFs older than ~90 days to Cool tier storage. This is a smaller saving but low risk.
